first.rationale: Two of the three symptoms (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, so the highest-leverage single slot is onboarding friction rather than a price response. memory_86 is the load-bearing record for that choice, so I verify it first: it reports completion and time-to-value lifts, which are proxies, not the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue, and it is 24 days old against a market that has since changed. I verify memory_73 second because competitive price pressure is the loudest signal and promotional pricing is the tempting alternative; its record claims acquisition and revenue lift but says nothing about retention, margin, or cohort quality, which is exactly where discount-led acquisition tends to destroy long-term qualified revenue. If verification shows memory_73 tracked durable retained revenue and memory_86 tracked only completion, I would revisit. Downstream risk on my own pick is real and I am flagging it: memory_31's field-cutting result and memory_86's shortening result both improve top-of-funnel proxies while potentially stripping qualification signal and admitting lower-intent accounts, and memory_44 warns that enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted path, so any simplification must be scoped to self-serve SMB and must not cannibalize the demo-request route. I therefore run a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, with success measured on downstream qualified revenue and 60-90 day retention rather than completion rate alone, plus a guardrail on enterprise demo-request volume. Referral incentives (memory_57) are set aside because they act on established customers and do not address the acquisition-stage decline; activation messaging (memory_91) is the strongest fallback if verification undercuts memory_86.

final.rationale: Verification resolved the decision. exp_86 held up on the dimension that matters: not just completion +13% and time-to-value -2.1 days, but 30-day retention +3%, meaning the shortened flow did not buy proxy gains by admitting worse-fit accounts. exp_73 collapsed under inspection: signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% were real but paired with 30-day retention -12%, and the source record explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidated summary of memory_73 had silently dropped that retention figure and the warning, which is precisely the failure mode I was budgeting against; the competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal in the room and following it would have traded next quarter's renewals for this quarter's signups. So I commit the slot to simplify_onboarding, which also addresses two of the three current symptoms at their shared source. Residual uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86's retention evidence stops at 30 days and my objective is renewal-cycle revenue, so a +3% 30-day number does not by itself prove durability across a full cycle. Separately, I am scoping this to the verified intervention — shortening the flow — and NOT to memory_31's cut-required-fields variant, which is a different manipulation, unverified, and the one most likely to strip qualification signal. Guardrails: self-serve SMB only, no change to the enterprise demo-request path given memory_44's pipeline-quality claim, primary readout on 60-90 day retained qualified revenue rather than completion rate, and a hold on broad rollout until a renewal cycle is observed. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout for that reason; activation_messaging (memory_91, still unverified) remains the next slot's candidate if this underdelivers.
